title: Digital Twin–Enabled Personalized Clinical Trials with Reliable and Explainable Data Pipelines using Organic Synthesis Model
abstract: The conventional clinical trials are frequently characterized by a lack of personalization, low levels of data reliability and low levels of interpretation, which restrict their use in real-life. The present paper suggests a personalized clinical trial model (DTOC) that incorporates organic synthesis-based drug modeling, multi-omics data fusion, and interpretable artificial intelligence (XAI)-based reliability pipelines with the help of digital twins. Physiology of every patient is simulated as a digital twin and provides an opportunity to simulate genomic, clinical, and quality-of-life signs in real-time. The organic synthesis module is the approximation of the drug-patient interaction on the molecular level, and the XAI layer increases the transparency and compliance with the requirements of GDPR and IEEE principles on AI ethics. Experimental validation with 500 patient datasets showed that it gained significant performance improvement, obtaining 92.3% and XAI reliability of 0.89 and improved in the reliability index by 16% over the baseline deep-learning-based methods. The suggested DTOC framework would guarantee reproducible, interpretable, and ethically consistent trial outcomes. Through the combination of customized drug production and explainable digital health simulation, this study enhances the future of customized clinical trials that can hasten the process of drug discovery, enhance health outcomes, and increase confidence in the AIdriven healthcare systems.

title: Detection and Compliance in Financial Management via 6G-Enabled Standardized AI-Powered Digital Twins
abstract: The quick development of financial technologies and digital transactions has made fraud detection and regulatory compliance more difficult. This study introduces a Financial Digital Twin with Explainable AI over 6G (FinDT-XAI6G) to enhance real-time fraud detection and compliance monitoring in financial systems. The proposed method leverages the ultra-low latency, high bandwidth, and pervasive intelligence capabilities of 6G networks to enable seamless synchronization between digital twins and real-world financial activities. Common modeling approaches ensure interoperability across financial firms, regulatory bodies, and auditing authorities. Embedded artificial intelligence systems continuously examine vast amounts of transactional data, behavioral patterns, and contextual indications to spot anomalies that could be signs of fraud. Financial firms may now fully and transparently explain automated judgments to regulators thanks to Explainable AI (XAI) modules that enhance interpretability. Blockchain-based audit trails also guarantee data integrity, accountability, and traceability across distributed infrastructures. The integration of 6G connectivity allows for real-time monitoring, cross-border compliance validation, and instant anomaly reporting, even in scenarios with huge data volumes. Comparative studies reveal that our 6G-driven digital twin approach significantly improves detection accuracy, reduces false positives, and expedites compliance verification when compared to traditional methods. Additionally, its scenario modeling capabilities enable the proactive assessment of emerging compliance risks in dynamic regulatory and commercial contexts. Overall, this study demonstrates how financial fraud prevention and compliance assurance in next-generation digital economies can be revolutionized by 6G intelligence-powered standardized, AI-integrated digital twins.

title: Explainable Digital Twin Framework for Aircraft Engine Maintenance
abstract: Growing dependence of modern aviation on aircraft engines underscores persistent challenges in balancing safety, reliability, and operational costs. Conventional maintenance practices, whether preventive or reactive, often prove inadequate, leading to premature component replacement, unscheduled downtime, and limited diagnostic transparency. To address these gaps, this study proposes an AI-driven digital twin framework that integrates predictive modeling, explainability, immersive visualization, and secure data management for aircraft engine maintenance. A Python-based simulator generates realistic IoT sensor streams replicating operational stresses, gradual degradation, and subtle anomalies, which are then analyzed using complementary machine learning models: an Isolation Forest for anomaly detection and a Random Forest Regressor for Remaining Useful Life (RUL) estimation. SHAP-based interpretability ensures that predictions remain transparent and traceable, a critical requirement for aviation applications. The framework further incorporates Unity 3D for interactive engine visualization and a Flutter mobile application for field-level accessibility, while blockchain-backed IoT logging and federated learning strengthen data integrity and collaborative scalability. Validation on synthetic datasets and the NASA C-MAPSS benchmark confirms improved robustness, with the Random Forest reducing RUL prediction error by over 30% and the Isolation Forest achieving an F1-score of 0.89 for anomaly detection. These results specify the framework’s potential as a transparent, scalable, and industry-ready solution for predictive maintenance in aviation, with adaptability to other safety-critical domains such as manufacturing and energy.

title: Trusted Medical AI: Blockchain-Backed Device Authentication With Digital Twin-Enhanced XAI for Lung Cancer Detection
abstract: Lung cancer remains the leading cause of cancer-related deaths worldwide, mainly due to late diagnosis and limited availability of expert pathologists. Although Artificial Intelligence (AI) and DT technologies offer promising avenues for early detection, their adoption in clinical settings introduces significant concerns around data security, system vulnerabilities, and model trust. In response, this paper proposes a novel, trusted medical AI framework that combines blockchain-based device authentication, explainable artificial intelligence (XAI), and DT technologies to enhance diagnostic accuracy, data integrity, and system resilience. The proposed system leverages ResNet for lung condition classification from CT scans, augmented by Grad-CAM for visual explainability, enabling clinicians to interpret AI-driven decisions confidently. A blockchain-based whitelist mechanism authenticates medical devices before data contribution, mitigating risks of tampered or unverified input. Furthermore, the framework integrates explainable digital twin visualization to simulate patient-specific predictions and embeds a vulnerability detection layer to identify and mitigate software flaws in medical IoT and DT components. This comprehensive solution addresses key challenges in real-world healthcare: ensuring data authenticity, interpretability, and cyber resilience, paving the way for secure, transparent, and trustworthy AI-driven diagnostics.

title: Explainability in Digital Twins: Overview and Challenges
abstract: Digital Twins are increasingly being adopted across industries to support decision-making, optimization, and real-time monitoring. As these systems and, correspondingly, the underlying models of their corresponding Digital Twins, grow in complexity, there is a need to enhance explainability at several points in the Digital Twins. This is especially true for safety-critical systems and applications that require Humanin-the-Loop interactions. Ensuring explainability in both the underlying simulation models and the related decision-support mechanisms is key to trust, adoption, and informed decision-making. While explainability has been extensively explored in the context of machine learning models, its role in simulation-based Digital Twins remains less examined. In this paper, we review the current state of the art on explainability in simulation-based Digital Twins, highlighting key challenges, existing approaches, and open research questions. Our goal is to establish a foundation for future research and development, enabling more transparent, trustworthy, and effective Digital Twins.

title: Synergic Use of Modeling & Simulation, Digital Twins and Large Language Models to Make Complex Systems Adaptive and Resilient
abstract: Modeling and Simulation (M&S) has long been essential for decision-making in complex systems due to its ability to explore strategic and operational alternatives in a risk-free manner. The emergence of Digital Twins (DTs) has further enhanced this by enabling real-time bidirectional synchronization with physical systems. However, constructing and maintaining accurate and adaptive models and DTs remains time- and resource-intensive and requires deep domain expertise. In this paper, we introduce an adaptive Decision-Making Framework (DMF) that integrates Large Language Models (LLMs) and Model-Driven Engineering (MDE) into the M&S and DT pipeline. By leveraging LLMs as proxy experts and synthesis aids, and combining them with MDE to improve reliability, our framework reduces manual effort in model construction, validation and decision space exploration. Here, we present our approach of DT construction and discuss how it improves agility, reduces expert dependency and can act as a pragmatic aid for making enterprise robust, resilient and adaptive.

title: An Explainable Neuro-Symbolic Rule Extraction Framework for Digital Twins
abstract: Digital twin monitoring systems suffer from interpretability limitations that hinder adoption in safety-critical industrial applications. We present the first neuro-symbolic rule extraction framework that transforms CNN-LSTM predictions into human-readable logical rules for transparent digital twin decision-making. Our approach introduces two key technical contributions: (1) the TENSOR (Temporal and Event-based Neural-to-Symbolic Extraction of Rules) algorithm that identifies multivariate temporal patterns in sensor data and converts them into Prolog-style symbolic rules, and (2) the DRCM (Dual-factor Rule Confidence Metric) that balances statistical correlation with predictive accuracy for rule validation. The framework processes high-confidence neural predictions to extract interpretable conditions including threshold checks, gradient analysis, temporal patterns, and feature correlations. Evaluation on synthetic industrial sensor data demonstrates improved accuracy over CNN-LSTM baselines while maintaining strong recall performance. Human evaluation with industrial engineers shows substantially higher interpretability ratings for rule-based explanations compared to neural-only outputs. The extracted rules achieve high confidence scores and provide actionable insights for operators, enabling validation of system recommendations through transparent logical reasoning. While current validation relies on synthetic data, this work establishes a methodological foundation for explainable AI in digital twin applications.

title: Standardizing Explainable and Secure AI in Digital Twin-Enabled e-Learning Systems
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) and Machine learning (ML) are increasingly used in energy and engineering systems, but these models must be fair, unbiased, and explainable. It is critical to have confidence in AI’s trustworthiness. ML techniques have been useful in predicting important parameters and in improving model performance. However, for these AI techniques to be useful for making decisions, they need to be audited, accounted for, and easy to understand. Therefore, the use of explainable AI (XAI) and interpretable machine learning (IML) is crucial for the accurate prediction of prognostics, such as remaining useful life (RUL), in a digital twin system, to make it intelligent while ensuring that the AI model is transparent in its decision-making processes and that the predictions it generates can be understood and trusted by users. By using AI that is explainable, interpretable, and trustworthy, intelligent digital twin systems can make more accurate predictions of RUL, leading to better maintenance and repair planning, and ultimately, improved system performance. The objective of this paper is to explain the ideas of XAI and IML and to justify the important role of AI/ML in the digital twin framework and components, which requires XAI to understand the prediction better. This paper explains the importance of XAI and IML in both local and global aspects to ensure the use of trustworthy AI/ML applications for RUL prediction. We used the RUL prediction for the XAI and IML studies and leveraged the integrated Python toolbox for interpretable machine learning (PiML).

title: ChainFedTwin: A Blockchain-Based Federated Learning Framework for Secure, Explainable Digital-Twin Collaboration
abstract: Federated Learning empowered Digital Twins may potentially provide a high-fidelity, privacy-preserving vision of distributed assets. However, verifiable trust, auditability, and interpretability at scale are difficult. This article presents ChainFedTwin, a seven-layered framework that tightly integrates federated learning with blockchain-supported governance and a multi-modal Explainable-AI layer. ChainFedTwin improves current DT frameworks by proposing advanced cryptographic methods, safe bias detection and protection mechanisms, and smart contract-based governance to realize security, privacy, and fairness upgrades. The XAI layer integrates SHAP and LIME for end-to-end interpretability and contains embedded bias detection per aggregation step with fairness validation services. Experimental evaluation on the NSL-KDD dataset proves that ChainFedTwin outperforms the baseline FedAvg algorithm substantially. Specifically, ChainFedtwin achieved a final test accuracy of 94.1% while FedAvg was 91%, an improvement of 3.1 percentage points. Apart from that, it converged to 90% accuracy in 48 iterations, a 47% iteration decrease from FedAvg’s 91 iterations, reflecting enhanced convergence speed and stability at the lower end final loss. While it causes about a 15% communication overhead due to privacy and auditing requirements, this is an acceptable compromise for increased security, trustworthiness, and interpretability in mission-critical DT applications.

title: Resource Orchestration for Industrial Collaborative Computing via Digital Twin Networks with Intelligence-Based Reinforcement Learning
abstract: Collaborative computing in the industrial Internet requires accurate digital models and effective scheduling. While digital twin networks (DTNs) support informed decision-making, modeling all network elements is costly and inefficient. To reduce overhead, we propose a user preference-driven DTN framework that dynamically identifies key nodes based on service requirements and performance feedback. Instead of statically modeling all nodes, this approach enables closed-loop, adaptive modeling aligned with task offloading efficiency. To further enhance decision-making, we introduce an intelligence-based reinforcement learning (IRL) framework that replaces scalar rewards with an "intelligence" metric, preserving multi-objective trade-offs and user preferences. The proposed approach facilitates interpretable and adaptive decisions in dynamic environments and is well-suited for communication-aware resource orchestration in edge-intelligent industrial networks. Simulation results show that our method outperforms traditional RL and baseline strategies across multiple performance metrics.

title: Interpretable AI for Built Environment Digital Twins: The Role of Tsetlin Machines
abstract: Digital Twin (DT) is a growing concept in industries such as manufacturing, energy, smart cities, and built environments. To bridge the digital and physical worlds, DTs often rely on state-of-the-art Machine Learning (ML) models. However, many ML models, like Neural Networks, are considered black boxes, making their decision-making processes difficult to interpret. To address this, the explainable AI paradigm has introduced methods like SHAP and LIME. Despite their effectiveness, interpreting model outputs remains challenging. This paper explores the potential of using Tsetlin Machines in built environment DTs to explain the detection of structural properties. The Tsetlin Machine has demonstrated strong performance even with limited training data while offering both local and global interpretability. Its rule-based approach provides transparent decision-making, making it a promising alternative to traditional black-box models in DT applications.

title: A Dynamic Assessment System for Nuclear Safety Culture Based on Digital Twin and Multi-Modal Fusion
abstract: To address the static and fragmented limitations in traditional nuclear safety culture assessment, this study proposes a novel evaluation framework integrating digital twin and multi-modal analysis. The system comprises two core modules: a safety culture digital twin and a multi-modal fusion engine, enabling dynamic perception and quantitative assessment of safety risks. The digital twin employs 3D virtual mapping to reconstruct equipment status, environmental parameters, and human behavior in real time, combining spatiotemporal prediction for visual risk simulation. It supports historical review and predictive analysis of safety culture evolution, forming an active "monitoring-warning-decision" chain. The fusion engine incorporates a domain-adaptive dynamic weight allocation mechanism to analyze questionnaires, operation logs, and meeting recordings. Enhanced by a nuclear safety knowledge graph, it integrates semantic, acoustic, and behavioral features to generate a causally interpretable evaluation matrix, significantly improving objectivity and practicality. Closed-loop verification confirmed the framework establishes a dynamic baseline model, enhances hazard identification timeliness, and facilitates a proactive safety management paradigm. This research offers a scalable technical solution for digital upgrades in highreliability industrial environments.

title: Real-Time Dynamic Job Shop Scheduling Method Based on Digital Twin and Deep Reinforcement Learning (TD3)
abstract: In highly dynamic and uncertain job shop environments, real-time scheduling faces complex challenges such as sudden tasks, equipment failures, and processing time fluctuations. To address this, this paper proposes a dynamic job shop real-time scheduling method that integrates digital twins with deep reinforcement learning (TD3). Initially, a Digital Twin Synchronization Module (DTSM) is designed to achieve a realtime virtual mapping of the physical shop floor by merging sensor data and modeling time delays. Next, a Priority-Aware State Encoder (PASE) is constructed, using a graph neural network to model the dynamic relationships between workpieces and equipment, and integrating workpiece urgency, equipment failure probability, and processing delay information to form a highdimensional state representation. Finally, a Multi-Head Action Selection Network (MH-ASN) is introduced, decoupling dispatching and sequencing decisions to achieve more fine-grained and interpretable scheduling control. Experimental results show that the proposed method significantly outperforms traditional heuristic algorithms and existing reinforcement learning-based scheduling models across multiple dynamic job shop benchmark scenarios.

title: Digital Twin Forecasting of Quorum-Sensing Associated Biofilm Microorganisms in Urban Wastewater Over a 30-Week Interval
abstract: Biofilms in wastewater systems contain dynamic microbial communities regulated by quorum sensing (QS), which governs adhesion, extracellular polymeric substance (EPS) production, stress tolerance, and developmental transitions. Forecasting QS-associated organisms is essential for anticipating biofilm formation and mitigating operational risks in wastewater infrastructure. In this study, we identified QS and biofilm-associated taxa present in a European wastewater metagenomic dataset: Vibrio harveyi, Vibrio parahaemolyticus, Pseudomonas aeruginosa, Escherichia coli, Salmonella typhi, Salmonella typhimurium, Bacillus subtilis, and Staphylococcus aureus. These organisms encode diverse QS and biofilm regulators across multiple bacterial lineages. From this broader QS-associated set, we developed an organism-specific, QS-aware digital twin focused solely on Pseudomonas, a dominant biofilm-forming genus in wastewater systems. Using the Q-net modeling framework, the model was trained on early-window observations and calibrated to perform short-horizon, end-point forecasting by predicting the final week of a 30-week interval. To ensure a stable conditioning window, the terminal signal was replicated prior to prediction. The digital twin demonstrated strong agreement between predicted and observed final-week abundance (R2=0.98), highlighting its effectiveness for end-point microbial forecasting. This streamlined and interpretable framework supports rapid microbial surveillance and provides a scalable tool for biofilm-aware operational decision-making in wastewater systems.

title: 13 Network Digital Twin
abstract: End-to-end automation in telecommunications is a challenging yet critical industry objective, representing collective vision for technology evolution in the coming years. Key enablers for achieving this include the expression and the translation of high-level business goals (e.g. intents) into actionable and impactful operations, the deployment and interaction between closed loops, real-time data management, the extraction of meaningful insights from data, ML-driven analytics and intelligence, and seamless orchestration and resource control. Automation processes must be transparent, reliable and robust. This book provides a comprehensive insight into the automation journey. It explores the vision of zero-touch, AI-native network and service autonomy, examining the key trends, catalysts, and technological advancements shaping this paradigm shift. It provides a comprehensive analysis of critical aspects such as data and knowledge management, security and trust, native AI/ML management, intent-based automation, and human-to-machine as well as machine-to-machine interfaces. By delving into advanced concepts such as data-driven, AI-powered analytics, semantic and decision models, network digital twins, and the role of natural language processing and large language models, the book bridges theory and practical application. It highlights how these innovations leverage and maximize intent-driven and closed-loop automation, enabling seamless, intelligent, and autonomous networks. Additionally, it identifies key areas where further research is needed to address existing gaps and unlock the full potential of these technologies. Ultimately, this book provides valuable insights, outlining the transformative potential of zero-touch, AI-native networks and paving the way for seamless, intelligent, and autonomous management of networks and services, driving innovation, efficiency, and new opportunities in the evolving digital landscape.

title: Heuristica: A Distributed System for Self-Reasoning Neuro-Symbolic Digital Twins in Ubiquitous Health Monitoring
abstract: Current AI in high-stakes health monitoring like cardiology suffers from opacity and an inability to integrate established medical knowledge. We present Heuristica, a distributed neuro-symbolic system designed to address these limitations by providing transparent, interpretable reasoning for clinical review. Its core is a novel, sub-100ms bidirectional feedback loop between a Neural Perception Engine (NPE) and a Probabilistic Reasoning Graph (PRG), featuring a sub-100ms core reasoning cycle. This allows the symbolic PRG to not only interpret but actively guide the NPE’s perception, fusing datadriven learning with medical logic in real-time. The system also features a privacy-preserving federated discovery protocol for aggregating relational insights across users without sharing raw data. Evaluations on cardiovascular benchmarks show significant accuracy gains (+15.3% F1-score), and promising clinical acceptance (89.2%) in a study with cardiologists, and can identify complex cardiovascular risk patterns validated on largescale retrospective data. By creating a symbiotic loop between neural perception and symbolic reasoning, Heuristica provides a blueprint for the next generation of trustworthy and interpretable AI for ubiquitous health systems.

title: A Lightweight and Explainable Digital Twin for Scene Monitoring Using Synchronized mmWave Radar and Vision Data
abstract: Digital Twins (DTs) are rapidly emerging as a transformative paradigm for real-time monitoring, simulation, and decision-making across domains such as smart mobility, industrial automation, and intelligent infrastructure. However, current DT implementations often rely on computationally intensive deep learning pipelines and vision-based sensing, which hinder their deployment in resource-constrained or privacy-sensitive environments. In this work, we introduce RadarVision-Twin, a lightweight, interpretable, and edge-deployable Digital Twin system that fuses mmWave radar and RGB camera inputs for real-time anomaly detection and feedback-driven visualiza-tion. Unlike traditional camera-centric systems, RadarVision-Twin leverages radar spectrograms to extract motion energy and camera frames to estimate edge density-two physically meaningful features that capture dynamic behavior and scene structure, respectively. These features are fused and fed into an XGBoost classifier, chosen for its efficiency and explainability, to detect motion anomalies in real-time. Our system supports synchronized multimodal visualization, live anomaly flagging, and operator feedback, forming a closed-loop DT that evolves with its environment. We validate our approach on a large-scale multimodal dataset comprising over 14,000 radar-camera frames, demonstrating that our fusion strategy achieves macro F1-scores of 98%, surpassing unimodal baselines. Furthermore, the system runs at low latency on commodity hardware and requires no GPU acceleration, making it suitable for embedded or edge deployments. By eliminating the need for deep models while maintaining interpretability and responsiveness, RadarVisionTwin paves the way for transparent, low-power, and privacy-aware Digital Twins in future 6G-enabled environments.

title: Optimizing Predictive Maintenance Based on Digital Twins Using Artificial Intelligence Tools
abstract: Predictive Maintenance (PdM) is a key industrial technique, yet traditional methods often lack the required accuracy and scalability. To address this, we propose a novel three-layer framework for Digital Twin-based Predictive Maintenance (PdMDT). The architecture integrates real-time data collection, a hybrid (data-driven and physics-based) digital twin for simulation, and an intelligent decision-making layer. It is built on novel learning methods such as CNN-LSTM and RF-LSTM in its decision-making layer. We validated the framework on an industrial water pump with 51 sensors, predicting faults with a 10-minute lead time. We developed two models: a CNN-LSTM with an attention mechanism (98.29% F1 score) that identifies key sensor contributions, and a lightweight RF-LSTM (98.91% F1 score) suitable for edge devices. The proposed PdMDT framework provides a scalable and interpretable solution applicable to real-world industrial environments. By enabling precise fault prediction and root cause analysis, it significantly reduces downtime and maintenance costs, advancing the implementation of smart manufacturing. While validated on a real industrial dataset, future work will extend the framework to live plant deployments to assess scalability and robustness in production environments.
justification: IC1 is explicitly satisfied: the paper proposes a “three-layer framework for Digital Twin-based Predictive Maintenance (PdMDT)” with a hybrid digital twin layer. IC2 is largely supported but not fully explicit as XAI: it claims an “interpretable solution” and describes an attention mechanism that “identifies key sensor contributions” plus “root cause analysis,” which are explainability-related, but it does not explicitly frame these as XAI/interpretability mechanisms within the DT itself beyond the decision-making model. IC3 is not explicitly satisfied: the abstract does not define any human roles (operator/maintainer/decision-maker) nor describe human-in/on-the-loop or human-centered interaction; it only mentions an “intelligent decision-making layer” without human involvement.

title: Autonomous Cyber Resilience via a Co-Evolutionary Arms Race within a Fortified Digital Twin Sandbox
abstract: The convergence of Information Technology and Operational Technology has exposed Industrial Control Systems to adaptive, intelligent adversaries that render static defenses obsolete. This paper introduces the Adversarial Resilience Co-evolution (ARC) framework, addressing the "Trinity of Trust" comprising model fidelity, data integrity, and analytical resilience. ARC establishes a co-evolutionary arms race within a Fortified Secure Digital Twin (F-SCDT), where a Deep Reinforcement Learning "Red Agent" autonomously discovers attack paths while an ensemble-based "Blue Agent" is continuously hardened against these threats. Experimental validation on the Tennessee Eastman Process (TEP) and Secure Water Treatment (SWaT) testbeds demonstrates superior performance in detecting novel attacks, with F1-scores improving from 0.65 to 0.89 and detection latency reduced from over 1200 seconds to 210 seconds. A comprehensive ablation study reveals that the co-evolutionary process itself contributes a 27% performance improvement. By integrating Explainable AI and proposing a Federated ARC architecture, this work presents a necessary paradigm shift toward dynamic, self-improving security for critical infrastructure.
justification: IC1 appears explicitly satisfied: the core contribution is an ARC framework operating “within a Fortified Secure Digital Twin (F-SCDT)” and the digital twin sandbox is central to the proposed co-evolutionary security setup. IC2 is only partially supported: the abstract states “By integrating Explainable AI,” but provides no explicit description of the explainability mechanism (what is explained, how, for whom, or how it is used/evaluated) within the digital twin context. IC3 is not explicitly satisfied: the abstract does not define any human roles (e.g., operator/analyst) nor describe human-in/on-the-loop or human-centered interaction; it focuses on autonomous Red/Blue agents and performance metrics. Because IC3 is missing and IC2 lacks explicit detail, the article cannot be included under strict Phase 2 rules.

title: Bayesian Digital Twin Framework for Anomaly Tracing and Simulation in Cyber-Physical Systems
abstract: Cyber-Physical Systems (CPS) are the foundation behind the automation industry, transport, and infrastructures, yet their rising complexity exacerbates sensitivity to anomalies that jeopardize safety and reliability. Anomaly detection techniques based on conventional wisdom are fragile, non-interpretable, and stiff in diverse settings. This work proposes a Bayesian Digital Twin (BDT) framework that combines high-fidelity simulation and probabilistic inference to ease scenario reproduction and traceability under uncertainty. Experimental validation on a vehicle as well as a smart grid testbed, involving over 1.2 million time-series measurements, included controlled faults such as sensor drift, actuator faults, cyber attacks, as well as communicate-traffic delays. It demonstrated localization error at 0.23, fidelity indices larger than 0.94, as well as convergence up to 36 iterations, significantly improved over Kalman filters as well as deep autoencoders. Scaler experiments up to 20,000 nodes confirmed sub-linear scaling up to inference as well as provided evidence to support deployability in real-time. Our results make Bayesian Digital Twins convincing interpretable as well as scaling agents up to the monitoring upof resilient CPS.
justification: IC1 is explicitly satisfied: the paper "proposes a Bayesian Digital Twin (BDT) framework" and validates it on CPS testbeds. IC2 is plausibly addressed via explicit interpretability language (it calls prior methods "non-interpretable" and claims the BDT is "interpretable"), though no concrete XAI mechanism is described. However, IC3 is not explicitly satisfied: the abstract contains no defined human roles (e.g., operator/decision-maker) and no explicit human-in-the-loop/on-the-loop or human-centered interaction mechanism. Under Phase 2 strict rules, missing IC3 requires exclusion.

title: AI-Enabled Digital Twin and Explainable Collaboration Analytics for Proactive R&D Projects Management
abstract: In the evolving landscape of defence Research & Development, timely delivery and optimal resource utilization are not just objectives — they are strategic imperatives. This paper proposes an AI enabled Digital Twin framework tailored for monitoring and forecasting activities in defence R&D initiatives. The solution is designed as a lightweight yet intelligent system, built entirely using accessible and scalable digital infrastructure, while embedding predictive analytics and explainable recommendations. By harnessing historical and live data from completed and active efforts, the model employs regression-based learning to estimate expected timelines for ongoing endeavors. Health scores are then derived by comparing actual elapsed time with AI-predicted progress, offering a transparent and actionable view of each initiative’s trajectory. Complementary visuals provide real-time insights into scheduling trends, progress deviations, and prioritization cues. These outcomes are not static metrics—they serve as living indicators within the Digital Twin, periodically updated to reflect evolving realities. The framework illustrates how even minimal digital infrastructure, when purposefully designed, can simulate twin-like behavior—delivering both macro-level foresight and micro-level guidance. By coupling predictive scheduling with explainable action triggers, the system empowers defence R&D teams to transition from reactive oversight to proactive governance, without relying on heavyweight platforms or proprietary tools.

IC2 is partially supported: it explicitly mentions "explainable recommendations" and "explainable action triggers" and calls the view "transparent and actionable," but it does not specify any concrete XAI mechanism (e.g., model explanations, feature attribution, rule extraction) beyond these claims. IC3 is not explicitly satisfied: while it says the system "empowers defence R&D teams" and supports "proactive governance," the abstract does not explicitly define human roles (operator/decision-maker) or describe a human-in-the-loop/on-the-loop interaction mechanism within the Digital Twin.

title: Efficient Torque Prediction for Digital Twins in Quarry Operations: A Data-Driven and Expert-Guided Approach
abstract: Quarry sites present unique operational challenges where the performance of heavy machinery is critical for maintaining efficiency and safety. In such environments, accurate torque prediction is essential for effective engine management and optimal task execution. This work addresses the torque prediction challenge for a wheel loader operating in quarry conditions by proposing a structured three-phase approach to feature selection that reduces model complexity while preserving predictive accuracy. In the first phase, features are selected based on domain expertise to capture the physical and operational realities of quarry machinery. A comprehensive set of features is then employed to establish a robust performance baseline. In the final phase, a data-driven analysis using SHapley Additive Explanations (SHAP) identifies the top five features that most significantly impact torque prediction. Model efficacy was validated via cross-validation, with R-squared and mean-squared error serving as the key performance indicators. Comparative analysis reveals that while SHAP-ranked features yield statistically optimal results, the expert-selected features are more aligned with the practical requirements of quarry operations. These findings support the design of efficient, interpretable digital twins for real-time decisions in challenging environments.
justification: IC1 appears satisfied: Digital Twin is central (title and abstract explicitly frame torque prediction for designing “interpretable digital twins” for real-time decisions). IC2 is satisfied: the abstract explicitly uses SHapley Additive Explanations (SHAP) to identify key features and explicitly claims support for “interpretable digital twins.” IC3 is NOT explicitly satisfied: while it mentions “expertise,” “expert-selected features,” and “practical requirements,” the abstract does not explicitly define a human role (e.g., operator/decision-maker) nor describe a human-in-the-loop/on-the-loop interaction mechanism within the digital twin system; thus inclusion cannot be confirmed under strict Phase 2 rules.

title: Patient Digital Twins for Dynamic Hospital Supply Chain Management AI-Based Predictive Resource Allocation
abstract: The fusion of Digital Twin (DT) technology and Artificial Intelligence (AI) holds great promise for the optimization of hospital supply chain management and resource allocation. This paper proposes a patient-specific digital twin framework aimed at forecasting hospital staffing needs and aiding supply planning by means of AI-based analytics. Preprocessing and modeling of hospital records that included admission information, medical procedures, room types, usage of supplies, and patterns of staffing were achieved by utilizing advanced machine learning algorithms. The strategy illustrated better performance compared to baseline strategies and had interpretability from feature importance analysis, which emphasized length of stay, critical care admissions, and specialized procedures as influential drivers of staffing requirements. The results show that the patient digital twin can optimize operational efficiency, avoid supply deficits, and facilitate evidence-based decisions. The suggested framework is consistent with the vision of contemporary healthcare supply chains in that it promotes resilience, flexibility, and smart resource management.
justification: IC1 is explicitly satisfied: the abstract states it “proposes a patient-specific digital twin framework” for forecasting staffing needs and supply planning. IC2 is explicitly satisfied: it reports “interpretability from feature importance analysis” identifying influential drivers. However, IC3 is not explicitly satisfied: the abstract does not define any human roles (e.g., operator/decision-maker) nor does it describe any human-in-the-loop/on-the-loop or human-centered interaction mechanism as part of the system; it only mentions “facilitate evidence-based decisions,” which is not an explicit HITL/HOTL specification.

title: Neuro-Symbolic Reinforcement Learning with Digital Twin Integration for Adaptive Load Frequency Control
abstract: Adaptive load frequency control (LFC) plays a vital role in stability of contemporary power systems as the incorporation of renewable energy sources and dynamic load fluctuations is increasing. LFC practices used in the traditional manner do not cope well with this form of ambiguity. This paper suggests a hybrid Neuro-Symbolic Reinforcement Learning (NSRL) system combined with Digital Twin (DT) simulations to allow real-time adaptive control of LFC systems. The framework is the integration of neural networks in dynamic pattern recognition, symbolic reasoning in interpretable decision-making, and reinforcement learning in continuous policy optimization. The digital twin offers an environment of safe testing and real-time adjustment. The experimental outcomes prove that the proposed framework provides an accuracy of 98 percent of frequency stability, which is more effective than the conventional LFC approaches and other AI-driven strategies considering frequency deviation, control signal accuracy and stability of the system. The integration of interpretable and adaptive implies a possibility of intelligent, confident, and robust power system operations of the framework that offers an immense improvement of the existing means of control.

IC2 is partially supported but not explicit within the DT context: the abstract mentions “symbolic reasoning in interpretable decision-making” and calls the framework “interpretable and adaptive,” but it does not explicitly describe any XAI/interpretability mechanism tied to the Digital Twin component specifically (e.g., DT-driven explanations, transparency features, or evaluation of explainability). IC3 is not satisfied: the abstract does not explicitly define any human roles (operator/decision-maker) nor describe human-in-the-loop/on-the-loop interaction mechanisms as part of the system.

title: Self-learning Cognitive Digital Twin Network of Autonomous Risk Intelligence and Predictive Fraud Protection in Next-Gen Banking
abstract: This paper presents the GenFedNet, a Self-Learning Cognitive Digital Twin architecture for autonomous risk intelligence and predictive fraud detection in the next-generation digital banking systems. Traditional fraud detection has been based on static rules or static machine learning models that are losing the war against fast-changing cyberfraud vectors. The proposed GenFedNet proposes cognitive digital twin, which can learn and adapt to the individual customers' behavior, transaction patterns, and contextual variations continuously via neuro-symbolic reasoning and federated optimization. Each twin simulates dynamic behavioral characteristics including spending rhythm, device usage, geo-location mobility and temporal variation to develop a unique behavioral fingerprint. Experimental results report performance of GenFedNet with 97% accuracy, 96% precision, 98% recall, and 97% F1-score by beating the experimental results of baseline models (SVM, Random Forest, CNN, FedCNN) with 12 to18% improvements. It also proves to be up to 40% less inference latency while retaining 95% security accuracy, which means faster decision making while dealing in real-time transactions. Both the stable anomaly and the consistent self-learning behavior of the model are represented by the trend of anomaly stability and fraud probability confidence, which validates the good prediction ability of the model. The system is scalable, privacy-preserving and interpretable, and fills the gap in today's banking ecosystem between operational intelligence and proactive security. This research will be extended with research on multi-modal behavioral fusion, blockchain-enabled model governance, and cross-institutional federated collaboration towards achieving advanced levels of transparency, fairness, and resilience in the defense against financial fraud.
justification: IC1 appears explicitly satisfied: the paper presents “GenFedNet, a Self-Learning Cognitive Digital Twin architecture” and describes per-customer twins simulating behavioral characteristics. IC2 is only weakly/ambiguously satisfied: the abstract labels the system “interpretable” but does not explicitly describe any explainability/XAI mechanism (methods, interfaces, or transparency approach); “transparency” is mentioned only as future work. IC3 is not explicitly satisfied: while customer behavior is modeled, the abstract does not define any human role (e.g., analyst/operator/decision-maker) nor any human-in/on-the-loop interaction within the system. Due to missing explicit human-role/interaction details and lack of explicit XAI mechanisms, it cannot be confidently included in Phase 2.

title: A Simulation-Based Digital Twin Framework for Predictive Maintenance of DC Motors
abstract: Predictive maintenance (PdM) of rotating machinery is a critical enabler of Industry 4.0; however, most industrial Digital Twin (DT) implementations require extensive sensor infrastructure, cloud connectivity, and capital investment— barriers that limit adoption in small-to-medium enterprises and early-stage research. This work presents a fully simulation-based Digital Twin framework for a DC motor PdM, designed as a computationally efficient, reproducible, and hardware-independent framework for early prototyping, education, and algorithm benchmarking. Developed in Python, the framework emulates temperature, vibration, and electrical degradation over 10,000 virtual operating hours using physics-informed models with stochastic variations. Maintenance decisions are triggered via threshold-based and probabilistic logic, thereby producing interpretable intervention cycles. To ensure external validity, the simulated vibration features were benchmarked against the NASA IMS Bearing Dataset, showing strong agreement in the early and mid-degradation phases (RMS correlation > 0.88) and identifying areas for late-stage behavior improvement. A cost– benefit analysis, expressed in USD, indicates 48.2% total lifecycle savings ($715.20 per motor) compared to reactive maintenance, with no unplanned downtime observed in the simulation. A sensitivity analysis across multiple policy scenarios demonstrates that the framework can be tuned for different maintenance philosophies without sacrificing operational reliability. By openly providing a complete codebase and structured simulation logs, this work addresses the gap between conceptual DT research and costly hardware-based implementations. The results establish a modular testbed intentionally designed as a simulation-only stage for developing and validating PdM algorithms, enabling low-risk, cost-efficient refinement before transitioning to hybrid, data-driven, and real-time industrial deployments.
justification: IC1 is satisfied: the work presents a “fully simulation-based Digital Twin framework” as the core contribution. However, IC2 is not explicitly satisfied: the abstract only mentions “interpretable intervention cycles” arising from threshold-based/probabilistic maintenance logic, but does not propose or discuss any explainability/XAI/transparency mechanism within the Digital Twin. IC3 is also not satisfied: there is no explicit definition of human roles (operator/decision-maker) nor any human-in-the-loop/on-the-loop interaction described. The paper therefore matches EC2 (DT-focused predictive/simulation maintenance without explicit explainability or human aspects).

title: Neural Enhanced Digital Twin Framework for Spatiotemporal Anomaly Detection and Predictive Insights in Smart Manufacturing Systems
abstract: A novel neural enhanced digital twin-based anomaly detection framework for smart manufacturing is presented that resolves problems including real-time assimilation of data, anomaly detection and predictive decision making. The proposed methodology, that combines the use of Graph Neural Networks for spatial modeling, Neural Ordinary Differential Equations for temporal dynamics, Differential Privacy for secure data management and Causal Inference for robust anomaly differentiation, leads to robust, and highly accurate and interpretable outputs. The implementation shows significantly better performance than baseline models (e.g. Logistic Regression, Random Forest, and LSTM) with 96.3% accuracy and 90.1%F1 score. Two key insights, namely machine-specific and time-dependent anomaly trends, are also demonstrated to show the system's applicability to a real time monitoring and operational optimization task. The results derived in this work provide the foundation for future work towards intelligent, secure, and adaptive digital twins in smart manufacturing.

IC2 is partially supported: the abstract explicitly claims "highly accurate and interpretable outputs" and mentions causal inference, but it does not explicitly describe an explainability/XAI mechanism (method, interface, or evaluation of explanations) within the Digital Twin beyond this claim. title: Data and Resource Management Challenges for Digital Twins
abstract: Digital twins are revolutionizing industries by providing real-time simulation, monitoring, and predictive analytics capabilities. However, their success hinges on overcoming significant data and resource management challenges. This keynote will explore four key issues critical to the advancement and scalability of digital twins. First, we will discuss the complexities of real-time data processing within the edge-cloud-IoT continuum, emphasizing the need for seamless integration and efficient resource allocation across distributed systems. Second, we will explore the use of Large Language Models (LLMs) for dynamic verification of the resilience of digital twins, highlighting their potential to enhance adaptability and real-time decision-making. Third, we will examine end-to-end monitoring strategies to ensure data integrity, transparency, and reliability, enabling trust in automated decision processes. Finally, we will address the integration of emerging computational technologies, such as quantum accelerators (e.g., Quantum Brilliance) and neuromorphic chips (like Intel Loihi and BrainChip Akida), at the edge network to accelerate data processing and improve the responsiveness of digital twins. This talk will provide insights into how these advancements can be leveraged to develop robust, scalable, and intelligent digital twin ecosystems, driving innovation and efficiency in realworld applications.

However, IC2 is not explicitly satisfied: while it mentions 'transparency' and 'trust' via monitoring and 'LLMs for dynamic verification,' it does not explicitly propose/implement/evaluate explainability/interpretability/XAI mechanisms within a DT context. IC3 is also not satisfied: no human roles (operator/decision-maker) or explicit human-in-the-loop/on-the-loop interaction mechanisms are described. Additionally, EC3 applies because it is explicitly a keynote talk (non-research talk format), which is excluded under Phase 2 strict screening.
